rows.title: Legal Persuasion and Argument
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Contrast and explain the difference between arguments of fact and arguments of law.
Recognize and appropriately respond to rhetorical tricks such as: emotional manipulation, inappropriate inferences, non sequiturs, incomplete arguments and incivility.
Structure a reasoned and researched persuasive argument both orally and in writing.
objectives: demonstrate the ability to distinguish arguments of fact from arguments of law;
demonstrate the ability to recognize both subtle and obvious arguments;
distinguish fact from opinion;
distinguish opinions from dicta in case law;
identify and analyze the primary issues in an argument;
identify and analyze the peripheral issues in an argument and determine what weight, if any, to give to these issues;
identify common fallacies and ambiguities in language and thought;
identify deliberate abuses and manipulations of argument, including, but not limited to, incivility and emotional hijacking;
demonstrate the ability to organize facts and analysis into a logical responsive argument, both orally and in writing.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Introduction to the Administration of Justice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the structure and process of American criminal justice, including the stages of criminal case processing.
Explain the relationship of criminal justice to social justice and how multiculturalism and diversity present special challenges to, and opportunities for, the American criminal justice system.
Compare and contrast the major components of the criminal justice system: police, courts, and corrections.
objectives: demonstrate an understanding the history, development, structure, and function of American police, courts, and corrections;
demonstrate an understanding of the theoretical explanations for crime and criminal behavior;
explain the sources and methods of collecting crime data, the emerging patterns of criminal activity, and the costs of crime;
demonstrate an understand the sources of criminal law;
compare and contrast the different crime control models of Administration of Justice;
trace the evolution of community policing and its impact on the crime rate;
explain the constitutional restrictions on police investigations and conduct;
explain the criminal justice process from arrest to adjudication to acquittal or sentencing and punishment;
explain the role and the constitutional basis for criminal defense attorneys;
demonstrate an understanding of history of corrections including probation, parole, and community corrections, as well as the goals of the correctional system;
compare and contrast the federal and state criminal justice systems;
analyze prisoner’s rights as they pertain to the Constitution and Bill of Rights;
identify and describe special issues in the criminal justice system involving juveniles, race and class;
demonstrate the ability to critically analyze criminal justice issues in literature, newspapers, and court decisions.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

discuss, describe, and state the main sources of criminal law and the reasons for the limits on criminal law and punishment in the U.S. Constitution and Bill of Rights;
Know the laws of arrest.
objectives: discuss the goals and characteristics of criminal law;
discuss the philosophical and historical evolution of criminal law, noting the role of the judiciary in its development;
write briefs concerning decisions rendered in appropriate cases;
explain the sources of criminal law and the concept of "police power";
demonstrate knowledge of the basic terminology, definitions, and theories of criminal law;
distinguish between substantive and procedural laws;
contrast criminal with civil liability;
explain the classification of crimes;
identify elements of offenses against the person, property, morals, and public peace and safety;
explain the capacity to commit crimes, causation, and culpability;
explain the laws of arrest and detention;
explain and discuss criminal defenses, legal justifications, and burdens of proof.

rows.title: Bus Engine Overhaul

outcomes: perform a cooling concentration level test, pressure test the cooling system, and inspect for leaks. Inspect all hoses and cooling system components for signs of deterioration;

rows.title: Fire Fighter I Academy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and explain through cognitive assessment the Fire Fighter I competencies on the following topics: fire fighter safety, communications, Incident Command System, fire tools and equipment, structural fire suppression, fire fighter survival, suppression of fires outside of a structure, wildland fire suppression, hazardous materials/WMD, and confined space awareness.

Demonstrate through individual psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, fire fighter safety competencies: donning, doffing and inspection of PPE; use, operation and maintenance of SCBA, including donning and doffing; responding on an apparatus; and operating an emergency scene. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique and safe operating procedures while using designated equipment in an expeditious manner.

Demonstrate through individual psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, communications competencies: operating a phone in a non-emergency situation; initiating a response to an emergency; operating fire department radios; and application of ICS in a tabletop exercise. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form and technique while using designated equipment in a safe and expeditious manner.

Demonstrate through individual psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, tools and equipment competencies: basic & intermediate knot & hitch ties using rope, webbing, prusik cords & carabiners; operation of hand and power tools; operation of portable electric and lighting equipment; and cleaning, inspection, and maintenance of fire tools and equipment. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures while using designated equipment in an expeditious manner.

Demonstrate through individual and team psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, structural fire suppression competencies: operation of fire extinguishers; water supply operations involving portable water tanks and hydrants; basic & intermediate ladder deployment operations; basic hose coupling, rolls, maintenance, carries, loads, lays & deployment for fire attack; utility control at emergencies; forcible entry through doors, windows, and walls; search and rescue of victims and firefighters, including use of support equipment; interior and exterior structure fire fighting operations; horizontal and vertical ventilation operations; salvage of room and contents with covers and equipment; and overhaul a fire scene. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures in an expeditious manner while using designated equipment as an individual and a member of a team.

Demonstrate through individual and team psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, fire fighter survival competencies: exit a hazardous area; determine a safe haven; and initiate a call for emergency assistance. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures in an expeditious manner while using designated equipment as an individual and a member of a team.

Demonstrate through individual and team psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, passenger vehicle fire fighting competencies: attack a passenger vehicle fire; avoid hazards; identify and control leaking flammable liquids; maintain protection from flash fires; overhaul all vehicle compartments; and extinguish the fire. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures in an expeditious manner while using designated equipment as an individual and a member of a team.

Demonstrate through individual psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, wildland response, equipment and safety competencies: assemble and prepare for response; don and doff wildland PPE; deploying fire shelters; inspect, maintain, and sharpen hand tools; assemble and use a back pump; assume the safe position for an air tanker drop; use the Incident Response Pocket Guide (IRPG). Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures while using designated equipment in an expeditious manner.

Demonstrate through individual and team psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, wildland fire suppression competencies: perform simple and progressive hose lays; use hand tools to construct fire line; perform mobile pumping; ignite and extinguish road flares and fusees; assemble and use a drip torch; prep and defend a structure in the wildland-urban interface; perform wet or dry mop-up operations; and demonstrate patrol principles, techniques, and standards. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures in an expeditious manner while using designated equipment as an individual and a member of a team.

Demonstrate through individual psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I hazardous materials/WMD competencies: identify hazardous materials, their potential hazards and appropriate personal protective equipment; identify container size, product or site identification number; and implement a hazardous materials response. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper technique & safe operating procedures while using designated resources in an expeditious manner.

Demonstrate through individual and team psychomotor assessment the following Fire Fighter I, hazardous materials/WMD first responder operational competencies: perform emergency, mass, and technical decontamination; don, work in, and doff chemical protective clothing; perform containment and control techniques to mitigate a hazardous materials/WMD incident. Performance of psychomotor assessments requires completion of all operations following proper form, technique & safe operating procedures in an expeditious manner while using designated equipment as an individual and a member of a team.
Complete a fire service structured oral interview including evaluation of a properly designed and formatted firefighter resume.

Complete 4 required and 2 random wildland certification examination skills according to the skills testing sheets designated by California State Fire Training.

objectives: don a structural personal protective ensemble so that all elements of the ensemble are worn according to manufacturer's guidelines, within 60 seconds;
don and activate a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) within 60 seconds, and demonstrate the ability to use the SCBA during emergency operations;
respond on apparatus to an emergency scene, correctly mount and dismount the apparatus, use seatbelts while the vehicle is in motion, and correctly use other personal protective equipment;

extinguish fires in exterior Class A materials, protect exposures, stop the spread of fire, avoid collapse hazards, effectively applied water, extinguish the fire, and preserve signs of the origin area(s) and arson;

attack a passenger vehicle fire, avoid hazards, identifying control leaking flammable liquids, maintain protection from flash fires, overhaul all vehicle compartments, and extinguish the fire, while operating as part of the team;
assemble and prepare for a wildland response so that arrival at the incident with the required personnel and equipment meets agency guidelines;

rows.title: Environmental Geology: Hazards & Disasters

outcomes: Design studies using the scientific method with hypothetical data collection strategies, monitoring protocols, and methods of analysis to assess natural disaster and hazard risks in various geologic settings.

objectives: Apply the scientific method to hypothesize about and analyze data from geologic settings to evaluate the potential for geologic hazards and disasters to occur.

Investigate the interactions of energy and resource usage and examine their impacts on human society, natural hazards and disasters.

Evaluate how fundamental geologic concepts and processes, such as plate tectonics, the rock cycle, climate change and the greenhouse effect impact and are impacted by natural hazards and disasters, both historically and in the present day.

Design strategies on how to mitigate the effect of geologic hazards on human populations in diverse geologic settings and evaluate suitable types of communication for conveying the risk of geologic hazards and disasters to the general public in these locations.

Investigate how natural hazards and disasters can both negatively and positively affect humans and the environment, compare and contrast hazard prediction and mitigation strategies in diverse geographic locations, and evaluate the possible effects of human activity on increases in the frequency of certain natural disasters.

Demonstrate eccentric training to strengthen tendons and ligaments to prevent overuse injuries.
